They help improve coordination among various agencies and build capacity to protect national maritime interests.

body.label: Exercise overview
body.text: Sea Vigil-26 is the fifth edition of the Pan-India Coastal Defence Exercise held from 11 to 19 November 2026, coordinated by the Indian Navy as the lead agency.

body.label: Phases of exercise
body.text: The exercise is conducted in two phases: the Coastal Defence and Security Readiness Evaluation (CDSRE) from 11 to 17 November, followed by the Sea Phase on 18 and 19 November.

body.label: Participants and scope
body.text: It spans the entire Indian coastline and Exclusive Economic Zone, involving all Coastal States and Union Territories, Indian Navy, Coast Guard, Coastal Security Police, Customs, and other maritime agencies.

body.label: Purpose and significance
body.text: Conceptualised in 2018 after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks, Sea Vigil validates maritime security measures and assesses national preparedness for maritime and coastal defence.

body.label: Coordination with ministries
body.text: The exercise is facilitated by multiple ministries including Defence, Home Affairs, Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Petroleum and Natural Gas, and Fisheries.

body.label: Link to TROPEX
body.text: Sea Vigil serves as a build-up to the Indian Navy's biennial Theatre Level Readiness Operational Exercise (TROPEX), together addressing maritime security from coast to high seas.

sections.heading: What is Sea Vigil-26 and how is it conducted?

body.label: Exercise details
body.text: The Indian Navy and Royal Navy of Oman conducted the 15th edition of their bilateral maritime exercise Naseem Al Bahr (Sea Breeze) to enhance interoperability and professional cooperation.

body.label: Harbour phase activities
body.text: Subject Matter Expert Exchanges covered Explosive Ordnance Disposal, Mine Countermeasure Operations, and Hydrography, facilitating knowledge and operational experience sharing.

body.label: Sea phase activities
body.text: Joint operations included Visit, Board, Search and Seizure drills and cross-deck operations between Indian Naval Ship Surat and Royal Navy of Oman Vessel Al-Mu’azzar.

body.label: Strategic importance
body.text: The exercise reflects close maritime partnership and supports India's vision of MAHASAGAR for mutual security and growth across regions.

Consider the following statements about the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) scheme:

body.label: Purpose of the scheme
body.text: The CGFMU provides credit guarantee coverage to lending institutions against default risk for loans extended to eligible micro enterprises under PMMY, overdrafts under PMJDY accounts, and loans to Self Help Groups with portfolios between ₹10 lakh and ₹20 lakh.

body.label: Guarantee coverage and fee
body.text: Guarantee coverage is linked to disbursement amounts for working capital and outstanding amounts for term loans, reflecting actual risk exposure; the guarantee fee has been reduced from 1% to 0.75% per annum for PMMY loans, with no change for SHGs.

body.label: Administration
body.text: The scheme operates through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC), which provides the guarantee to lending institutions.

sections.heading: What is the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units scheme?

body.label: Extension approval
body.text: The Union Cabinet approved the continuation of the CGFMU scheme for five years up to March 31, 2031, covering the XVIth Finance Commission cycle (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31).

body.label: Corpus and loan facilitation
body.text: A corpus of ₹5,000 crore has been approved to facilitate PMMY loans amounting to ₹12.6 lakh crore over the next five years.

body.label: Impact so far
body.text: Since its launch in January 2016, the scheme has catalyzed the sanctioning of over 60.36 crore loans totaling ₹43.34 lakh crore, enabling a new generation of entrepreneurs to access collateral-free loans.

sections.heading: What are the recent developments regarding the CGFMU scheme?

body.label: Promotes entrepreneurship
body.text: By providing collateral-free loans, the scheme helps aspiring entrepreneurs who previously could not access formal banking credit to start and grow their businesses.

body.label: Supports financial inclusion
body.text: The scheme extends credit guarantees to loans under PMMY, overdrafts under PMJDY, and loans to Self Help Groups, thereby supporting vulnerable and underserved sections of the economy.

body.label: Catalyst for MSME growth
body.text: The CGFMU acts as a catalyst for micro, small, and medium enterprises by mitigating lending risks for financial institutions, encouraging more credit flow to the sector.

body.label: Economic growth
body.text: Improved access to transportation hubs and reduced travel times can enhance productivity and stimulate local businesses near new stations.

back2basics.text: Regional health cooperation involves countries working together to improve public health outcomes by sharing resources, expertise, and coordinated responses to health challenges. It helps in disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, and building resilient health systems. Such cooperation can include joint action plans, shared digital health initiatives, and collaborative research in traditional medicine, enhancing healthcare access and security across borders.

2026-11-12-am-b9b884286a.deck: The inaugural BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting in Colombo saw unanimous adoption of a Joint Ministerial Statement and a Revised Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030). This marks a key step in regional health collaboration, with India offering expertise and hosting a Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine.

body.label: Joint Ministerial Statement
body.text: The meeting unanimously adopted a Joint Ministerial Statement reaffirming commitment to accessible, affordable, quality healthcare and regional health security across BIMSTEC countries.

body.label: Revised Plan of Action
body.text: The Revised BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Public Health (2026–2030) was adopted, outlining cooperation on disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, digital health, traditional medicine, One Health, and healthcare workforce development.

body.label: Regional Centres of Excellence
body.text: The meeting welcomed initiatives including a BIMSTEC Centre of Excellence for Public Health in Sri Lanka, a Centre of Excellence on Tropical Medicine in Thailand, and India's commitment to host a Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine at ITRA, Jamnagar.

sections.heading: What were the key outcomes of the first BIMSTEC Health Ministers’ Meeting?

body.label: Leadership and Expertise Sharing
body.text: India highlighted its healthcare transformation and offered to share expertise in primary healthcare, digital health systems, and public health infrastructure with BIMSTEC countries.

body.label: Healthcare Infrastructure Support to Sri Lanka
body.text: India exchanged an MoU to supply 100 fully-equipped ambulances to Sri Lanka under a grant assistance of approximately USD 5.28 million, enhancing emergency medical response.

body.label: Support for Primary Healthcare in Sri Lanka
body.text: India announced support for 50 Medical Kiosks/Health ATMs to strengthen Sri Lanka’s primary healthcare services, integrating point-of-care diagnostics with telemedicine.

body.label: Bilateral Engagements
body.text: India held bilateral meetings with Sri Lanka and Nepal to deepen healthcare cooperation, reflecting strong historical and cultural ties and the Neighbourhood First policy.

sections.heading: How is India contributing to regional health cooperation under BIMSTEC?

body.label: Strengthening Regional Health Security
body.text: The cooperation enhances disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, and coordinated responses to cross-border health threats, crucial for regional stability.

body.label: Advancing Universal Health Coverage
body.text: The joint commitment supports Sustainable Development Goal 3 by improving access to quality health services and building resilient health systems.

body.label: Promoting Traditional Medicine
body.text: India’s hosting of the Centre of Excellence in Traditional Medicine fosters collaborative research and preservation of traditional knowledge across the region.

body.label: Digital Health Innovation
body.text: The meeting envisaged a BIMSTEC Digital Health Framework to promote telemedicine, interoperable electronic health records, and AI in diagnostics.

sections.heading: Why does this regional health cooperation matter for India and the BIMSTEC region?

back2basics.text: A CEPA is a type of free trade agreement that covers trade in goods, services, investment, and other economic cooperation areas. It aims to reduce tariffs and non-tariff barriers, facilitate market access, and promote economic integration between the partner countries.

2026-11-12-am-f2fc41a5b7.deck: India and Canada held discussions on November 11, 2026, to advance negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) aimed at boosting bilateral trade and investment. body.label: Participants
body.text: The discussions were held between India's Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal and Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu, who led the Canadian delegation.

body.label: Focus of talks
body.text: Both sides focused on advancing negotiations for the India-Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) to boost two-way commerce and investments.

body.label: Key objectives
body.text: They emphasized the importance of a balanced and mutually beneficial agreement that provides meaningful market access, leverages economic complementarities, and creates new trade and investment opportunities.

body.label: Shared commitment
body.text: Both ministers reaffirmed their commitment to elevating the India-Canada economic partnership, with CEPA acting as a catalyst for deeper commercial engagement and shared prosperity.

sections.heading: What was discussed in the India-Canada trade talks?

body.label: Enhancing bilateral trade
body.text: The CEPA aims to increase two-way trade and investment flows, which can contribute to economic growth and diversification.

body.label: Leveraging complementarities
body.text: By leveraging the complementary strengths of the two economies, the agreement can open new sectors and markets for Indian businesses.

body.label: Strengthening economic ties
body.text: The pact is expected to deepen commercial engagement, reinforcing India’s economic diplomacy and international partnerships.
